name: Crew Habitat Module
description: Pressurized multi-layer composite living quarters housing astronauts, command consoles, and baseline radiation shielding.
educational_explanation: Space habitats must maintain a ~101.3 kPa or exploration-atmosphere pressure shell, thermal control loops, and micrometeroid/radiation protection. Upgrading adds water-wall shielding and crew capacity comfort.

name: Photovoltaic Solar Array
description: High-efficiency triple-junction sun-tracking solar wings that convert solar irradiance into electrical energy (kWh).
educational_explanation: Solar arrays generate clean electricity without fuel, but output drops sharply during lunar night shadows or Martian dust storms, and regolith dust accumulation requires regular cleaning.

name: Regenerative Battery Bank
description: High-density lithium-ion and regenerative fuel-cell energy storage unit to buffer eclipse periods and peak loads.
educational_explanation: Without adequate energy storage, surplus daytime solar power is wasted and the base suffers life-support brownouts during low-sunlight periods.

name: Oxygen Generator Assembly (OGA)
description: Splits water molecules (2H2O -> 2H2 + O2) via solid polymer electrolysis (and CO2 Sabatier/MOXIE processing on Mars) to produce breathable oxygen.
educational_explanation: Producing oxygen on-site saves massive launch weight, but electrolysis demands continuous electrical power and purified water feedwater—demonstrating a classic ECLSS engineering trade-off.

name: Closed-Loop Water Recycler (WPA)
description: Distills, filters, and catalytically oxidizes cabin humidity condensate and crew wastewater back into potable water.
educational_explanation: Water is the heaviest consumable in human spaceflight. Recycling 85–95% of crew water reduces external extraction demand at the cost of electrical power and filter maintenance.

name: Hydroponic Aeroponic Greenhouse
description: Controlled-environment agricultural dome using LED spectrum lighting to grow dwarf wheat, leafy greens, and tubers while scrubbing CO2.
educational_explanation: A greenhouse produces fresh food and supplemental oxygen via photosynthesis, boosting crew health—but it is a heavy consumer of both electrical power (LEDs) and irrigation water.

name: Regolith-Berm Radiation Shelter
description: Heavily shielded subterranean vault lined with sintered regolith and polyethylene water walls for solar storm protection.
educational_explanation: During Solar Particle Events (SPEs), standard habitat hull walls may not block high-energy protons. Dedicated storm shelters drastically cut acute radiation dose.

name: Deep Space Communication Array
description: High-gain Ka-band parabolic dish and space-weather telemetry receiver connecting the outpost with Earth Mission Control.
educational_explanation: Reliable communications provide advance warning of solar flares, allow science data downlinks, and keep crew connected with flight surgeons and engineers on Earth.

name: Crew Medical & Countermeasure Bay
description: Equipped with radiation dosimetry, telemedicine diagnostics, autonomous surgical care, and resistive exercise hardware.
educational_explanation: Microgravity/partial-gravity deconditioning, minor trauma, and radiation stress require dedicated medical countermeasures to sustain astronaut performance.

name: Robotics & Maintenance Workshop
description: 3D additive manufacturing bay and robotic servicing depot that automatically slows wear and restores facility condition.
educational_explanation: Abrasive lunar and Martian dust degrades seals, bearings, and solar panels daily. On-site spare part fabrication and preventative maintenance prevent cascading system failures.

name: Pressurized Rover & ISRU Garage
description: Deploys pressurized surface rovers to prospect and extract water-ice regolith from shadowed craters or subsurface glaciers.
educational_explanation: Even a 93% efficient water recycler loses 7% of water over time, plus water split for oxygen. In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) rovers replenish water reserves from local ice deposits.

name: Planetary Science & Geology Lab
description: Analytical spectrometer and astrobiology laboratory for core samples, closed-loop ecology trials, and mission science objectives.
educational_explanation: The core purpose of human outposts on the Moon and Mars is scientific discovery—studying planetary evolution, searching for biosignatures, and testing technologies for deep space.
